title: Shake a drink with ice in a sealed Boston shaker and open it without spilling
instruction: Seal the shaker and shake the drink with its ice until mixed, then open the shaker, leaving the drink in the large tin standing on the table, without spilling any.
context: Bartenders and home cocktail makers seal a two-piece Boston shaker, shake the drink with ice to mix and chill it, then strike the seam to break the seal and pull the tins apart to pour: a seal that opens mid-shake sprays the drink across the bar. Sealed, the shaker is 28.7 cm long and its tins jam together, so it is shaken with a hand on each tin and opened with one hand holding the large tin.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A two-piece Boston shaker stands upright on the centre line, 22 cm forward: a catalogue pair of 18/8 stainless steel shaker tins sold to work together (Acopa 28 oz full-size tin, item 176SHKTSL28, and Acopa 18 oz half-size tin, item 176SHKTSL18), at their listed sizes. (1) The large tin: 177.8 mm (7 in) tall, 92.1 mm (3 5/8 in) across the top and 63.5 mm (2 1/2 in) across the bottom, outside, with 0.5 mm walls, so 91.1 mm across inside at the mouth (830 ml brim-full: its 28 oz); 186 g; loose. (2) The small tin: 133.4 mm (5 1/4 in) tall, 87.3 mm (3 7/16 in) across its rim and 60.3 mm (2 3/8 in) across its bottom, outside; 145 g. It is set straight into the large tin's mouth, mouth down, on the same axis, and rests where its rim meets the large tin's wall all round: 23.4 mm below the mouth, where the large tin's inside has narrowed (0.161 mm of diameter per mm of depth) from 91.1 mm to 87.3 mm. Resting there it is not sealed: it lifts off with 0.8 N more than its own weight. Pressed 1.0 mm further in, to 24.4 mm, where the large tin is 87.15 mm across inside, the rim is 0.16 mm tight in the taper, a friction press fit: the shaker is sealed. Sealed, it is 28.7 cm long and weighs 0.51 kg with its contents. (3) The drink, in the large tin. In a real trial it is 120 ml (127 g): 90 ml of room-temperature water, and 30 ml of simple syrup (sugar and water 1:1 by weight, about 50 °Brix) dyed blue, poured in slowly down the side so that it lies as a layer under the water. In simulation it is 24 blue plastic beads 8 mm across, 5.3 g each (127 g in all), each standing for 5 ml. (4) Four ice cubes, 2.5 cm, 14 g each, on top of the drink: real ice from a standard tray, straight from a -18 °C freezer, in a real trial; rigid cubes of the same size and mass in simulation. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, except the seal rule and the shaking count, which cover the whole trial. Each tier states its real-trial measurement and its simulation measurement. 0.0 if the large tin was ever tipped more than 30 degrees while the shaker was not sealed (real trial: judged from the video as the tins parting or drink escaping while it was tipped; simulation: the small tin not pressed home to 24.4 mm deep, or pulled out of that seat past its hold since), if any ice cube ends outside the tins, or unless the large tin ends standing upright on the table (tilted less than 10 degrees). Otherwise: 1.0 with the drink mixed, at most 5 ml spilled and the shaker open (the small tin lifted off, its rim at least 3 cm from the large tin's mouth). Real trial: the top and bottom samples read within 1.0 °Brix of each other, and the tins with what is in them weigh at most 5 g less than before. Simulation: shaken while sealed, that is, while sealed and tipped past 45 degrees, at least 6 changes of direction along the shaker's axis, each after a leg of 2.5 cm or more, and the ice cubes reaching alternate ends of the shaker (a cube's centre within 9 cm of that end's floor, touching that tin) at least 8 times in all; and at most 1 of the 24 beads out of the tins. 0.5: the same, but with up to 15 ml spilled (real trial: at most 15 g lost; simulation: at most 3 beads out). 0.25: mixed (real trial) or shaken (simulation) as for 1.0, with at most 5 ml spilled, but the shaker left sealed. Else 0.0. Real-trial measurements: before the trial both tins with the drink and ice are weighed on a kitchen scale (1 g resolution); after it both tins, wherever they ended, are wiped dry outside and weighed again with whatever is in them, and 1 g lost is 1 ml spilled (melting ice changes nothing). Within 1 minute of the shaker being opened (by a person, if the robot did not), 1 ml is drawn with a pipette from 1 cm under the drink's surface and 1 ml from the large tin's floor, and each is read on a handheld Brix refractometer (0 to 32 °Brix, 0.2 °Brix divisions; a reading off the top of the scale counts as unmixed). Unshaken, the top reads about 0 and the bottom is off the scale; mixed, both read about 13 to 15. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Empty, rinse and dry the tins, then refill the large tin: 90 ml of water, 30 ml of blue syrup layered under it, four fresh 2.5 cm ice cubes; set the small tin back in its mouth, unsealed. In simulation the beads and cubes start in the large tin again.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). No liquid: the 120 ml drink is 24 rigid 8 mm beads (5 ml, 5.3 g each), so mixing is measured only in a real trial; the sim scores sealed strokes that carry 4 rigid ice cubes end to end. Tins: 32-sided, listed sizes, walls 2 mm and floors 5 mm (real 0.5 mm). The fit is a slide joint, 15 N per mm past first contact; sealed at 24.4 mm it holds 8.7 N, plus a 41 N vacuum that a 10 N push at the seam vents. Cameras 1280 x 704.
